The short question that falls for consideration in the present  appeal is whether the High Court, vide its impugned judgment and  order dated 15.10.2019, was justified in award  interest at the rate of 15% p.a. on the amount of damages, held to  be payable to the respondent-land owners for their land admeasuring  65 Kanals and 5 Marlas, situated at village Khandipahari, Tehsil  Kulgam, Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir.
3. The facts are not in dispute.

The possession of the subject  land was taken at least with effect from 09.03  earlier, and the land was handed over to the Army authorities  through Military Estates Officer, Srinagar, for construction of  residential units for married personnel of 15 Corps of the Army.

4.
The respondent-land owners being dissatisfied with the amount of compensation, filed Reference under Section 18 of the State Act, which was forwarded to the District Judge, Anantnag on 30.03.2002.

The Reference Court accepted the land owners claim in part and, vide an Award dated 08.05.2006, enhanced the compensation to Rs. 1,75,000/- per kanal for Abi Land and Rs.1,58,000/- per kanal for Maidani Land.

Pursuant thereto, the District Judge, Anantnag passed a fresh Award on 09.07.2014 maintaining the same rate of compensation as was awarded through the previous Award, relying upon the commercial value of the subject land.

The High Court, vide the impugned judgment, has accepted  3 the aforesaid claim, whereby the respondent-land owners have been held entitled to additional interest at the rate of 15% p.a. as damages on the compensation determined from the date  dispossession, i.e., 09.03.1978, till the date the de under Section 6 of the State Act was published on 06.06.1989.

Needless to say, the rate of compensation, as determined by the High Court, having been accepted by both the parties, has attained finality.

11. The subject land, the value whereof has bee determined by the High Court, was admittedly utilized by the Union of India for a public purpose of paramount importance, for which eventually it has been acquired.
There is, thus, no dispute that the respondent-land owners were dispossessed and were deprived of the fruits and benefits of their land for the per 09.03.1978 to 06.06.1989.
The award of compensation, for the said period as damages by the High Court, is also not under challenge before us.

It seems to us that the grant of additional interest  4 amount is an integral component of the expansive expression `compensation as defined under the State Act or the corresponding provisions in the Central Act, which was in force at the relevant time, i.e., the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

That being so, the determination of the rate of additional interest by the High Court,
keeping in view the principles evolved by this Court from time to time, including those laid down in Balwan Singh vs. Collector (LA)
(2016) 13 SCC 412, may not warrant any interference by this Court in exercise of its powers under Article 136 of the Constitution.

12. We, therefore, in light of the peculiar facts and circumstances of this case, are not inclined to interfere with the rate of additional interest awarded by the High Court on the amount of compensation held to be payable to the respondent-land owners with effect from 09.03.1978 till 06.06.1989.

13. For the reasons aforestated, we do not find any merit in Union Of India vs Raja on 5 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9735091/
4 this appeal which is, accordingly, dismissed.
